drivers.label: Data Centers segment net sales
drivers.source: Base: Modine 8-K 2026-07-24 Ex.99.1 recast segment table, FY2026 Data Centers net sales $1,108.2M [src 6]. Q2 FY27 release + slides [src 75, 76]; call 2026-11-04 [src 77]. Investor Day 2026-11-18 deck slides 35-37, 42-45, 47, 58 [src 112]; >$4B to one customer CY2027-2029 (FY2026 10-K [src 7]); hyperscaler capex [src 119]; Dell'Oro [src 120]; peers [src 116, 117, 118].
drivers.derivation: INVESTOR DAY UPDATE 2026-11-19 (ground-up from lines in service x output per line, bounded by demand; company FY29 targets are cross-checks in guidance_check, never the level). CAPACITY: Modine runs 13 chiller lines now and is committed to 20 (CEO Neil Brinker, Q2 call [src 77]); the Investor Day line plan (slide 42, CEO Neil Brinker [src 112]) is chiller lines 4 / 20 / 25, AHU lines 3 / 6 / 8 and indoor lines 10 / 17 / 19 for FY25 / FY27 / FY29 on 7 / 14 / 14 facilities, and slide 43 puts revenue capacity at $2B (FY27, current), $3-4B at full efficiency (FY28) and $6-7B with further expansion (FY29). Lines in service: +3 at the start of Q3 FY27 and +4 at the start of Q4 FY27 (13 -> 20, the committed FY27 plan; split ESTIMATE); FY29: capacity units grow by the mix-weighted slide 42 line growth, (0.45 x 5/20 chillers + 0.23 x 2/6 AHU + 0.19 x 2/17 indoor) / 0.87 = 24.3% (FY26 mix weights slide 35; other and aftermarket assumed to follow), added in four equal steps at the start of Q1-Q4 FY29 (no start dates are given, so the latest timing the slide allows, moderately conservative). A new line makes 60% / 85% / 100% of a mature line's output in its first / second / later quarters (ESTIMATE: 1H27 margins were hit by 'ramp inefficiencies', slide 48, and 'there's often margin compression in the middle of a ramp', CEO Neil Brinker [src 77]). OUTPUT PER LINE: Q2 FY27 reported 439.7 on 13 lines = 33.8 a quarter [src 75] (supply-hit: shortages of critical components from Q1 FY27, slide 44); five supplier LTAs, vertical integration and pass-through mechanics are 'securing our FY28 and FY29 supply needs' (slide 44 [src 112]), so mature output rises in a straight line to 40.0 a quarter by Q1 FY28 and stays there through FY29. 40.0 = 91% of the slide 43 full-efficiency midpoint ($3.5B / 20 lines / 4 = 43.75) and 107% of its low end (37.5): the base takes ramp efficiency below management's full-efficiency claim (moderately conservative, rule 0c: Modine missed its one numeric quarter comment, the CFO's Q2 FY27 DC margin 'back between 19% and 20%' (15.4% reported; Q1 FY27 had no numeric guide), and FY28 adds no facilities, so the gain must come from throughput); no per-line gain is credited in FY29 although slide 43's $6-7B FY29 capacity implies ~$260M a line-year (65 a line a quarter) on 25 lines (the deck does not say what delivers it beyond 'expand capacity at existing sites'; sized as an alternative). Effective lines Q3 FY27 14.80 / Q4 17.95 / Q1 FY28 19.40 / Q2-Q4 FY28 20.00 / FY29 20.73, 21.76, 22.98, 24.19; output 35.88 / 37.94 / 40.00. RESULT: Q3 FY27 531.1 (+78.5% y/y), Q4 681.0 (+69.4%): FY27 2,000.4 (+80.5%, inside the +80-90% FY27 guide on the Q2 FY27 deck, slide 12 [src 76] (the Investor Day deck gives no FY27 sales guide), and at the deck's $2B FY27 capacity); FY28 3,176.0 (+58.8%; 91% of the $3.5B full-efficiency midpoint); FY29 3,586.6 (+12.9%). DEMAND CHECK (the demand-led build below is above this capacity in every forecast quarter but Q1 FY28, 749 vs 776, whose estimate sits on the supply-hit Q1 FY27 base and so understates; capacity binds): the $4B LTA with a major hyperscale customer starting in FY27 (slide 58, CFO Mick Lucareli [src 112]; 10-K: CY2027-2029, 'no assurance' [src 7]) = ~333.3 a quarter on an even phasing, 42% of FY28 DC sales; the customer stack (slide 45) shows four hyperscalers, three colocation, one neocloud and 'excess demand' above the $3-4B FY28 and $6-7B FY29 capacity bars (no figures); hyperscaler 2026 capex guides ~$730B, about double 2025's $376B, with Alphabet's CFO saying capex will 'increase significantly in 2027' [src 119]; Omdia DC cooling market $15B in 2025 to $46-78B in 2030 (slide 37), Dell'Oro DCPI +22% a year 2025-2030 with thermal the fastest-growing segment [src 120]; MOD FY26 DC $1.1B = ~7% of Omdia's 2025 market, FY28 at 3,176.0 = ~11-14% of a CY2027 market of $23-29B (slide 37's $15B 2025 at 25% a year, the rate that reaches its $46B 2030 low end: 15 x 1.25^2 = 23.4, to its 38% CAGR: 15 x 1.38^2 = 28.6); at $0.8-1.0M of content per MW (slide 36) FY28 equals ~3.5 GW of fully equipped capacity. Peers confirm demand above supply in DC thermal: Vertiv Q3 2026 organic orders >+100%, organic sales +55% [src 116]; nVent organic +44%, backlog $2.6B [src 117]; Trane Americas Commercial HVAC backlog ~+80% [src 118]. Cross-checks, not used: FY29 DC target $4.5-6.5B (slide 47) and capacity $6-7B: ours 3,586.6 is below both (guidance_check); Zacks consensus FY3/28 sales $4.14B (pre-Investor Day, retrieved 2026-11-17 [src 111]) less CHVAC ~1.2B = ~2.94B DC, below ours; Modine's Jan-2026 FY28 DC target $2.5-2.9B (src 92) is below ours, and its FY26 $1.0B target was beaten (1,108.2). BEFORE: FY27 2,000.0 (Q3 499.6 / Q4 712.1, the $2B capacity split by the CFO's quarter shape), FY28 3,469.4 / FY29 3,500.0 (20 lines x 43.75 through FY29).

drivers.label: Data Centers segment adj. EBITDA margin
drivers.source: Base: recast FY2026 DC adj. EBITDA $214.7M / $1,108.2M = 19.4% [src 6]; Q1-Q2 FY27 [src 4, 75]. Call 2026-11-04 [src 77]. Investor Day deck slides 42, 44, 48, 49 [src 112]; peers [src 116, 117, 118].
drivers.derivation: INVESTOR DAY UPDATE 2026-11-19 (built from the slide 48/49 margin bridges, CEO Neil Brinker [src 112], at the LOW END of every component, with fixed-cost absorption computed on our own volumes; the 2H27 20-21% and FY29 22-24% targets are cross-checks). Start: 1H27 15.1% (slide 48; reported Q1 14.8% / Q2 15.4% [src 75]) on 1H average sales 394.1 a quarter. VOLUME (fixed-cost absorption): the deck's own bridges imply fixed costs of ~16-26 a quarter: slide 48 gives +150-250bp of volume for 2H vs 1H, and slide 49 +200-300bp for FY27 -> FY29; with management's sales (2H ~631 a quarter vs 1H 394; FY27 ~512 vs FY29 ~1,375) both imply F = 16-26 (F x (1/394 - 1/631) = 1.5-2.5pt; F x (1/512 - 1/1,375) = 2.0-3.0pt). The base takes the low end F = 16.0 a quarter, half of it facility-level (14 facilities in FY27 and FY29, slide 42) and half scaling with installed lines (13 -> 20 -> ~24.9 units), and applies it to OUR sales: margin before items = 19.16% - fixed / sales. PRICING: +250bp from Q4 FY27 (half in Q3 for the approval lag): slide 48 pricing +200-300bp 'to cover increased costs' and slide 44 cost sharing / pass-through 'to offset higher costs in the second half of FY27 and beyond'; the CFO's 'call it 250 basis points catch-up' on the Q2 call (CFO Mick Lucareli [src 77]). SG&A: +50bp (slide 48 low end; half in Q3). FY28-29: operational excellence +100bp and commercial excellence (cost-adjustment mechanisms) +50bp, the slide 49 low ends, phased in evenly over the eight quarters; less the 12.5 a year of stranded corporate costs the CFO says move into Data Centers (src 77; corp_cost). No margin credit for the 2H labor/overhead recovery beyond absorption, and no allowance for the deck's 'excess demand' pricing. RESULT: Q3 FY27 17.30% / Q4 19.18% (H2 18.35% vs the deck's 20-21%), FY27 17.09% (deck 18-19%), FY28 19.68%, FY29 20.57% (deck 22-24%; Q4 FY29 20.93%). Peers: Vertiv Q3 2026 adjusted operating margin 25.2% [src 116], nVent adjusted return on sales 22.1% [src 117], Trane Americas adjusted EBITDA margin 23.5% [src 118]: our FY29 EBITDA margin sits below all three operating-level margins. Record: the CFO's Q2 FY27 margin expectation 'back between 19% and 20%' (Q1 call, CFO Mick Lucareli [src 23]) came in at 15.4% [src 75], 3.6-4.6 points short (the Q1 drop to 14.8% was one the CFO said was expected, so it is not counted as a miss [src 23]), so every component is taken at its low end. Supersedes the 2026-11-18 cost-recovery build (Kilian card): that build took no volume absorption; the Investor Day bridge quantifies it and the cost-recovery path stays as an alternative. BEFORE: Q3 16.62% / Q4 17.87%, FY28-29 ~17.76% (Q2 + 250bp; FY26 19.37% - 375bp + 250bp - redeploy).

drivers.derivation: INVESTOR DAY UPDATE 2026-11-19 (slides 29-30, Michael Mahan presenting Commercial HVAC [src 112]; targets are cross-checks). H1 FY27 reported 15.46% (Q1 15.90% / Q2 15.06% [src 4, 75]; deck 1H27 15.5%). Q3 FY27 16.9% = Q3 FY26 16.16% + the CFO's '50 to 100 basis points year-over-year improvement in Q3' midpoint (declared guide use, CFO Mick Lucareli [src 77]). H2 FY27 = H1 + 200bp, the sum of the LOW ENDS of the slide 29 2H components (pricing +100, mix +50, integration +50bp; the slide's stated range is 250-450bp, so the build sits 50bp under its bottom): H2 17.46%; Q4 FY27 = the rest of that H2 after Q3 = 17.98% (closes the must-card row: Q4 now rests on the slide 29 component build, not on 'another big lift'). FY27 16.47% vs the deck's 17-18% (below: 1H was 15.46% on our figures, and the low-end components). FY28-29: each quarter = the same FY27 quarter + the HVAC peers' consensus EBITDA margin gain (Trane, Carrier, Johnson Controls medians +0.75pt next year, +0.69pt the year after, MarketScreener [src 113, 114, 115]) + 25bp a year of acquisition synergy (slide 30 synergy capture 50-100bp FY27 -> FY29, low end; MOD-specific: integration of CDI and L.B. White, slide 63): FY28 17.45%, FY29 18.39% vs the deck's FY29 20-22% (volume/mix 100-200, operational 100-150, synergy 50-100bp). Moderately conservative (rule 0c): Q2 FY27 margin was flat y/y at 15.1% when the CFO had expected a higher margin [src 122]; Modine's own 80/20 record (+710bp company margin FY22-26, slide 14) argues the deck's bridge can be met, which is the upside alternative. Trane Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 21.4% [src 118] shows where scaled commercial HVAC sits. BEFORE: Q4 FY27 19.0% (unsourced, must-card), FY28 ~17.50%, FY29 ~18.18% (peers' gains only).

drivers.source: Base: FY2026 corporate -$62.6M (recast Ex.99.1 [src 6]); Q1-Q2 FY27 [src 4, 75]; slide 20 [src 76]; CFO stranded costs [src 77]; Investor Day slide 8 [src 112]; Trane corporate [src 118].
drivers.derivation: INVESTOR DAY UPDATE 2026-11-19 (built from the post-spin cost base and a scale cost; replaces the flat -15.0 a quarter the gate found unsupported). Allocated costs: Investor Day slide 8 (CEO Neil Brinker's opening section, slides 5-18 [src 112]) gives FY26 RemainCo adj. EBITDA $301M, so FY26 continuing corporate = 301 - DC 214.7 - CHVAC 162.4 = -76.1 against the segment table's -62.6 [src 6]: ~13.5 a year (13.5 / 4 = 3.375 a quarter) of corporate cost formerly charged to Performance Technologies now sits with RemainCo (slide 8 is the base used; the slide 20 recast gives 13.1 for FY26 [src 76], 3.275 a quarter, a 0.4 a year difference; the Q2 FY27 2.8 read from the slide 20 image is no longer used). Structural post-spin core: Q2 FY27 segment-table corporate -15.3 [src 75] + 3.375 allocated = 18.675, less the CFO's temporary stranded costs ('$10 million-$15 million', midpoint 12.5 a year = 3.125 a quarter, CFO Mick Lucareli [src 77]) = 15.55 a quarter. Q3/Q4 FY27 -19.30 each = 15.55 + the stranded costs still to be redeployed in H2 ('$7 million-$8 million', 3.75 a quarter [src 77]). FY28-29: core 15.55 + 1.37% of each quarter's sales above the Q2 FY27 level (725.2): a scale cost on added sales (ESTIMATE). The CFO's 'we are controlling the spending as a percentage of sales' [src 77] was said of total-company SG&A (which then included $14.1M of spin-off expenses), not of the corporate line, so it supports only that overhead spending is managed against sales; the corporate line's own scaling rests on the peer intensity: 1.37% = Trane's unallocated corporate expense on revenue in Q3 2026 (92.3 / 6,759.7 [src 118]), a scaled commercial-HVAC company's corporate intensity, used as the cost of each added dollar of sales (ESTIMATE). Stranded costs move into Data Centers from FY28 (12.5 a year in dc_margin = the midpoint of the CFO's 'about $10 million-$15 million of temporary stranded costs' a year, which he says will be 'reabsorbed ... through the data center growth' and 'fully absorbed by next fiscal year'; the '$7 million-$8 million' he names 'to redeploy into the data center business' is the H2 FY27 half-year impact, booked in corporate for Q3/Q4 FY27; CFO Mick Lucareli [src 77, 122]), so total EBITDA keeps them. FY27 -76.9, FY28 -81.8 (2.00% of sales), FY29 -88.2 (1.88%). Cross-check: the deck's FY29 targets taken together (total 19-21% on $5.7-7.7B vs DC 22-24% on $4.5-6.5B and CHVAC 20-22% on $1.25B) leave ~-155 to -220 for corporate and eliminations, ~2.7% of sales: higher than ours (not used: a residual of rounded ranges). Estimate, confidence medium. BEFORE: Q3/Q4 FY27 -18.7, FY28-29 -15.0 a quarter flat (-59.9 a year; must-card row).

judgment_calls_history.question: Compress MOD exit multiples for the market-implied NVIDIA financing channel?
judgment_calls_history.context: MOD's exit multiples (k=0.8 rule on the 2026-10-23 peer tables: 13.57x EV/EBITDA, 21.25x P/E) predate the AI-financing slide and Huang's resignation. FIN fell 18.1% since the peer tables and 10.3% on the resignation day, so the market-implied financing part of MOD's multiple is -8.2% (since 10-23) or -4.7% (day only). MOD printed inside the window (Q2 FY27 on 11-03; FY3/27 consensus fell 6.55 -> 6.25 by 11-12), so the price move is not purely a multiple move; the regression takes only the part that loads on FIN. It is a call because FIN also carries general AI-capex-cycle risk and MOD's own abnormal move on the day was ~0. The loading's 95% band is 0.21-0.70 (-3.8% to -12.6% since 10-23).
